message.reasoning_content:
Analyze and record description. Key risk: threshold 2.414213562373095 is 1+sqrt(2) truncated; Cephes uses more. Notably reciprocal uses tl.maximum(magnitude,1.0) guard which changes value for magnitude in (2.414,∞)? maximum(magnitude,1.0)=magnitude when magnitude>1, so fine. But when upper, reciprocal = -1/magnitude — fine. Potential bug: sign handling with x=0: value negative of 0 fine. Bigger risk: FP32 rational approximation accuracy vs 1e-6 abs tolerance across all FP16 values including ±65504 (atan≈π/2). Also the middle threshold 0.66 vs Cephes Morebits? Cephes uses x > 2.4142 and x > 0.66 exactly. The atan constant: 1.5707963267948966 = π/2, correction okay. The atan constant for upper range in Cephes: atan(1/x) subtracted from π/2 — here value = angle + local_angle where local_angle is negative (reduced<0, correction sign) — okay. Risk: FP32 rounding at extreme values: atan(65504)≈π/2−1/65504≈1.5707963267948966−1.5e-5. FP32 π/2 rounding error ~1e-7ish. Also the accuracy of rational approx with FP32 arithmetic could exceed 1e-6? Cephes double coeff ~1e-8 error; FP32 accumulation error ~ square*r... maybe ~1e-7? Risky. Also line 40: where(x<0, -value, -?) -0 fine.

One suspicious detail: reciprocal = -1/max(magnitude,1.0): for magnitude>2.414 max is magnitude, ok; guard only for... never matters. Fine.

Also 0.66 boundary: reduced uses centered for magnitude>0.66; Cephes threshold is 0.66 too? Cephes: if x > 2.414213562373095 then y=π/2-atan(1/x) style. Actually Cephes uses MORE bits... The thresholds match typical Cephes. Also boundary input exactly 2.414213562373095 (not representable in FP16 anyway) — FP16 so fine.

Key risk: |x| exactly ~0.66 not FP16 issue. Record description.
